text:
maria: FYI pushed a prototype for a 'sliding-probabilistic-admit' heuristic to address KV-cache-driven OOMs during continuous batching. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/789

vikram: brief explainer? how is it different from headroom thresholds we already have?

maria: short: instead of hard per-batch headroom we compute an admission probability p = base * (1 - kv_frac)^alpha * exp(-queue_len/beta). small requests get higher base. sliding window over last 30s of kv occupancy -> smooths out spikes.

olivia: can you paste the config snippet? want to run it in canary infra.

maria: sure, proto config (untested):
```
admit_policy: sliding_probabilistic
base_prob_small_tokens: 0.95
base_prob_large_tokens: 0.4
kv_window_seconds: 30
alpha: 2.0  # amplify kv occupancy effect
beta: 12.0  # queue len damping
min_prob: 0.05
max_batch_tokens: 4096
```

jax: ran microbench on g5.2x yesterday. With current static headroom (old) p99 latency = 64ms, p99.9 = 220ms; with a naive probabilistic admit i tried, p99 stable but saw a 12% increase in median because we ended up serializing more small requests. need kernel-aware routing.

maria: noted. the intent is to bias small requests so we don't serialise big ones. but we also switch kernel paths if kv_frac > 0.8 (fast-path disabled) -> fall back to kv-light kernel that is more memory-frugal but slower per-token.

perf-bot: [auto-profile] canary run 4001234599: throughput -6%, p95 +8%, OOM events: 0 (previously 3 in 24h). link: https://perf.internal/reports/4001234599

vikram: numbers look promising on OOMs but regressed tail. proposal: add a transient 'probabilistic-kernel-favor' that favors kv-light kernel when queue_len > q_thresh for admitted batches. that keeps admission high but reduces memory per batch.

olivia: i worry about oscillation: frequent kernel switches might thrash CUDA kernels and hurt p99. we should add a sticky TTL per-gpu for kernel decisions and measure context-switch cost.

maria: agreed. plan: sticky window 10s, and hysteresis on kv_frac change of at least 0.06 before switching. also add a cooldown on batch admission changes (only update admit prob every 250ms) to avoid feedback storms.

jax: i can run a focused perf sweep: compare static-headroom vs sliding-prob (no kernel-switch) vs sliding-prob + kernel-switch + sticky TTL. will collect p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and KV mem walk traces.

devops-bot: Deploy started: runtime/canary/sliding-prob/2026-03-18T15:23Z by maria.

vikram: test matrix requests: (1) synthetic small-token-heavy workload, (2) mixed with long chats, (3) prefix-heavy KV reuse workload. Also track eviction rate and avg kv fragment size.

maria: thanks. if sweep shows >10% tail reg we back off to safer alpha and raise min_prob. i'll add telemetry hooks for kv_frac, admit_prob, selected_kernel, and kernel_sticky_until to the per-request trace.

olivia: also add a lightweight admission log sample to S3 for debugging: one in 1k requests. include request_token_len, kv_frac, queue_len, decision, kernel.

jax: uploading first batch of traces now, will tag team when done.

maria: short-term acceptance criteria for canary: OOMs -> 0, p99 <= old p99 * 1.12, 0 severe regressions on mixed workload. if passes, we roll to 10% for 24h.

vikram: optional: consider a tiny learned model that predicts per-request eviction risk based on kv_keyset overlap and request length. can come later.

maria: noted, file follow-up. thanks all :thumbsup:
